Lessons.Title: Rewriting Quadratic Expressions in Factored Form (Part 1)
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: reverse distributive multiplication for monic quadratic trinomials with positive integer factor constants, using an area diagram to find numbers whose sum is b and product c. Original Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 7 Lesson 6 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/7/6/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/7/6/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source uses rectangle area puzzles and does not yet rely on a universal factoring algorithm.

Independent expression x²+10x+24. Seek two positive integers with sum10 and product24:4 and6. Thus x²+10x+24=(x+4)(x+6). A decomposition has central square x², strips4x and6x, and corner area24; each part is accounted for.

Another original trinomial x²+11x+30 factors into (x+5)(x+6), since5+6=11 and5×6=30. At x2, the first trinomial equals4+20+24=48 and factors6×8=48. Algebraic distributivity, not merely sample equality, establishes identity.

Student task: create an area diagram, test multiple factor-pairs for c, explain why both sum and product must match, factor a second expression and critique a pair with correct product but wrong sum. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 for diagram, factor search, expansion verification and error-analysis reasoning.

For x²+10x+24, positive factors4 and6 satisfy sum/product.
